stem: Design a 13-nucleotide forward primer and a 13-nucleotide reverse primer that amplify only the highlighted sequence.
teach: Forward primer = the first 13 nt of the highlighted region, copied as written 5'->3'. Reverse primer = the reverse complement of the last 13 nt. Both are written 5'->3', which is why the reverse one looks backwards compared with the top strand.

stem: Design a set of primers that will amplify the underlined sequence. Your professor asked for Tm as well: aim for 54-60 C and try to end the 3' end on G or C.
teach: Same rule at any length. The lecture adds two design points: keep both primers within a few degrees of each other in Tm, and prefer a G or C as the final 3' base so the polymerase starts on a stable pair.

stem: Which of the restriction enzymes in the table could be used to cut this DNA?
teach: Scan the top strand for each 6-base site. GGATCC appears once, at position 15. The near-misses matter: BclI is TGATCA and BglII is AGATCT, so both share the central GATC but differ in the flanking base. Read all six bases before you commit.

stem: Circle the restriction enzyme recognition sequence that will produce blunt ends when cut.
teach: The cut arrow sits dead centre of TGGCCA (3 bases each side), so both strands break at the same point: blunt. C↓CTAGG is cut after 1 base, leaving a 4-base 5' overhang: sticky.
